summary.bn: চার বিটের একটা সংখ্যা (০–৯) নিয়ে ৭-সেগমেন্ট ডিসপ্লের ঠিক সেগমেন্টগুলো জ্বালায়
summary.en: Takes a four-bit number (0 to 9) and lights the right segments of a seven-segment display

simplified: The chip answers at once: the time a real one takes is left out.

LT̅ LOW lights every segment; otherwise BL̅ LOW lights none. While LE is LOW the segments follow A to D; while LE is HIGH they keep the number held when it went HIGH. 10 to 15 light nothing. As in its datasheet, 6 is drawn without its top bar and 9 without its bottom bar.

It is a CMOS 4000-series chip and works from 3 to 18 V. Its outputs give current to a common-cathode display; each segment still needs its own resistor. An output is modelled as the supply or ground through about 50 Ω, like the 74HC chips; a real CD4511's HIGH is a little below its supply.
An input is HIGH above 70 % of the supply and LOW below 30 %; in between it keeps its last level. These are typical figures, not measured.
It is placed across the centre gap with pin 1 at the bottom left, and cannot be turned round.
